'''Robert K. Logan''' (born August 31, 1939), originally trained as a [[physicist]], is a [[media ecology|media ecologist]].

==Career==
He received from [[MIT]] a [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] in 1961 and a [[PhD]] in 1965 under the supervision of [[Francis E. Low]]. After two post-doctoral appointments as a research associate at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] (1965-7) and the [[University of Toronto]] (1967-8), he became a physics professor in 1968 at Toronto until his retirement in 2005. He is now professor emeritus.<ref name=UT>[http://www.physics.utoronto.ca/people/homepages/logan/ "Robert K. Logan"], [[University of Toronto]] faculty page.</ref>  He is a fellow of [[St. Michael's College, Toronto|St. Michael's College]], [[University of Toronto]], the [[Origins Institute]] at [[McMaster University]] and Institute of Biocomplexity and Informatics at the [[University of Calgary]].

While active at the [[University of Toronto]], in addition to math-based physics courses he taught an interdisciplinary course &ndash; ''The Poetry of Physics'' &ndash; which led to his collaboration with [[Marshall McLuhan]], and his research in media ecology and the evolution of language. His best known works are ''The [[Alphabet Effect]]'' &ndash; based on a paper Logan co-authored with McLuhan &ndash; which develops the hypothesis that the [[alphabet]], codified law, monotheism, abstract science and deductive logic form an autocatalytic set of ideas that developed uniquely between 2000 BC and 500 BC between the [[Tigris-Euphrates river system]] and the [[Aegean Sea]]; ''The Sixth Language: Learning a Living in the Internet Age'' which deals with the hypothesis that speech, writing, math, science, computing and the Internet form an evolutionary chain of languages; ''The Extended Mind: The Emergence of Language, the Human Mind and Culture'' develops a model for the [[origin of language]], the human mind and culture using ideas from ''The Sixth Language''.

Logan has also been chief scientist at Strategic Innovation Lab at [[OCAD University]] in Toronto, Ontario since 2007, and a senior fellow at the university's Strategic Innovation Lab (sLab).<ref name=ocad>[https://ocad.academia.edu/RobertKLogan "Robert K. Logan"], faculty page at [[OCAD University]]</ref> Part of his work at OCAD involved a language-based project to change popular attitudes about the environment, which resulted in the coining of the word "[[depletist]]".

In September 2010, Logan founded the McLuhan Legacy Network, a non-profit organization based in Toronto dedicated to renewing the legacy of Marshall McLuhan and celebrating the centenary of McLuhan's birth in 2011.<ref>[http://figureground.ca/2011/02/01/the-mcluhan-legacy-network/ "The McLuhan Legacy Network"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131028001542/http://figureground.ca/2011/02/01/the-mcluhan-legacy-network/ |date=2013-10-28 }} on ''Figure/Ground''</ref> 

In 2020 Logan launched the journal New Explorations: Studies in Culture and Communication as the founding editor. The journal has been published on average twice annually since then through 2026 with the last issue Vol 5 #2 available at [https://jps.library.utoronto.ca/index.php/nexj/issue/view/3000 https://jps.library.utoronto.ca/index.php/nexj/issue/view/3000.]

Logan's work is influenced by [[Marshall McLuhan]], [[Harold Innis]], [[Alvin Toffler]], [[Stuart Kauffman]] and [[Terrence Deacon]].

==Awards and honors==
''The Sixth Language'' won the Suzanne K. Langer Award for Outstanding Scholarship in the Ecology of Symbolic Form in 2000 from the Media Ecology Association,<ref>[http://www.media-ecology.org/awards/mea_recipients.html "Past MEA Award Recipients"] on the Media Ecology Association website</ref> and in June 2011 Logan received the Walter J. Ong Award for Career Achievement in Scholarship from the same Association.<ref>[http://www.media-ecology.org/awards/2011_awards.html "The 2011 MEA Awards"] on the Media Ecology Association website</ref>
